sentences.text: The paper directly answers the question. SPECTER does not require any citation information at inference time. Unlike many prior works, at inference time, our model does not require any citation information.
The authors also explain why this matters: the model can embed new papers that have not yet been cited.
Citation information is used only in the citation-based pretraining objective, formulated as a triplet loss.
Training instances are triplets, but this construction only involves citations while building training data. Where the query paper P Q cites the positive paper P + and not the negative paper P −.

The model itself takes a single paper as input and produces its representation from the pooled Transformer output over the paper text. The triplet loss aggregates three such per-paper embeddings: d(P A , P B ) = ‖v A − v B ‖₂.
This design yields a feature-based embedding that can be applied to downstream tasks without task-specific fine-tuning, which is consistent with embeddings computed from text alone.

The citation signal is still empirically important for that pipeline, even though inference itself does not require it: the authors stress that the citation-based pretraining objective is critical, and replacing it with vanilla SciBERT lowers performance on all tasks.

As an additional methodological detail, the authors say that they removed incoming citations from development and test queries because those citations would not be available at test time in production. This confirms the inference-time setup.
